title: Germany's Merz under pressure as AfD eyes second state win
summary: Exit polls have the far-right AfD leading the Social Democrats in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and the Left Party ahead in Berlin. DW has more.
byline: Richard Connor, Kieran Burke, Roshni Majumdar

image.caption: Merz insists Germany is capable of reformImage: Christian Mang/REUTERS

blocks.text: Chancellor Merz says election outcome in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania a 'disaster'
Chancellor Friedrich Merz set a defiant tone after blows sustained by his conservative CDU party in the votes in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin.
"The result in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania cannot be talked away, it’s a disaster," Merz said in a statement.
He pointed out to Germany's economic problems and deepening divisions, saying that "the answer cannot be a return to the good old time."
"The answer must be to make out country fit for the future," he told reporters. "The reforms have to happen."
"These reforms are a cure against the authoritarian poison," the chancellor said, in apparent reference to the far-right AfD party.
"We are taking over this responsibility. I am taking over this responsibility because I want to bring our country forward," Merz added.
